'''Pikobi''' were fast-moving, flightless [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavians]] which were native to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name="Field Guide" /> and could also be found on [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]],<ref name="TCW|Voices">{{TCW|Voices}}</ref> the jungles of [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]]<ref name="SWE" /> and the sewers of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="TJWKTM">{{TCW|The Jedi Who Knew Too Much}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
[[File:Pikobis2-woswfg.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Pikobis hunt for fish.]]

Pikobis specialized in fishing and probing through the mud for small prey such as [[gullipud]]s, [[nyork]]s, [[Nuna/Legends|common nuna]] chicks, [[Nuna/Legends|dwarf nunas]], [[Mee/Legends|mees]], and small crustaceans. Being waders and runners, they could cover long distances quickly both in and out of the water. Pikobis also had long, pointed beaks lined with sharp teeth that were used to spear and hold onto slippery prey which it usually swallowed in one gulp.<ref name="Field Guide" />

[[File:Pikobi.jpg|thumb|A Pikobi in the swamps of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].]]
These creatures possessed large, webbed feet which they used to create shadowy areas to attract fish, keen eyesight, external ears which were different from those of most reptavians, and a long tail for balance while it ran. Pikobis could shed their tail when attacked. The tail would grow back quickly, even sometimes forked. Scientists have also studied the Pikobis for medical purposes.<ref name="Field Guide" />

The Pikobi traveled in pairs or groups of five to six. The mother would lay its eggs in the sand and upon birth, the young could already walk and swim.<ref name="Field Guide" />

==Behind the scenes==
The general build of Pikobis does resemble small theropods such as ''Sinosauropteryx'' (124-122 mya), although they lack the feathers.<ref name="Drawing from the Past: How Prehistoric Creatures Influence Star Wars Designs">{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-past-how-prehistoric-creatures-influence-star-wars-designs|text=Drawing from the Past: How Prehistoric Creatures Influence ''Star Wars'' Designs|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref>
